text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.5% today to close at $151.54, extending a strong two-week rally of over 10%. The stock has climbed sharply since October 23rd, when Brent crude hit a six-month high above $116 a barrel amid escalating Middle East tensions—particularly the standoff between Iran and Saudi Arabia, including Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure. With U.S. oil now trading at $107.89 and global prices at $115.22, the broader energy sector is benefiting from the supply risk premium these geopolitical events have created.

The timing matters: even though oil ticked slightly lower on October 26th after Saudi and Iranian officials met to discuss de-escalation, the underlying price levels remain elevated, and the threat of supply disruptions—especially to critical Saudi export and refining capacity—continues to support higher crude valuations. This regional instability has already started reshaping global energy markets and benefiting U.S. energy producers, according to reporting from the period, making major integrated oil companies like ConocoPhillips direct beneficiaries of the higher price environment.
